(항우연 제공) 한국항공우주연구원은 이 누리호 5차 발사 성공을 기념해 나로우주센터 우주과학관 돔영상관 운영을 재개한다고 27일 밝혔다. 돔영상관에서는 항우연이 자체 제작한 누리호 5차 발사 영상을 선보인다. 관람객은 지난 7일 성공적으로 발사된 누리호의 비행 모습을 발사 현장에서 돔영상으로 체험할 수 있다. 성층권 태양광 무인기(EAV-4) 비행 영상도 함께 상영해 항공 분야 연구개발 성과를 소개한다. 이와 함께 인류의 화성탐사 도전을 담은 'One Step Beyond', 햄스터 과학자의 우주 모험을 그린 '3-2-1 Liftoff', 외계행성 탐험을 소재로 한 '콤콤: 미지의 외계행성 콤콤을 찾아' 등 우주탐사 콘텐츠 3종도 상영한다. 시설 재정비를 마친 돔영상관은 총 124석 규모로, 4K 화질 프로젝터와 에어젯·포그 등 4D 특수효과 시스템을 갖춰 몰입감 있는 관람 환경을 제공한다. 항우연은 내달 30일까지 하루 2회 무료 시범운영을 실시하며 영상·음향·특수효과의 안정성과 관람객 편의성을 점검할 예정이다. 이후 개선사항을 반영해 12월 1일부터 정식 운영에 들어간다. 이상철 항우연 원장은 “누리호가 발사된 바로 그 자리에서 발사의 순간을 돔영상으로 다시 만날 수 있도록 준비했다”며 “국민이 우주개발 성과를 더 가까이에서 접할 수 있는 공간으로 우주과학관을 계속 발전시키겠다”고 말했다. 이인희 기자 leeih@etnews.com

items.t: SpaceX locks in $40B GPU financing deal with Apollo
items.d: The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets.
items.fullText: SpaceX has reached a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing for AI chips and related data center equipment, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing Monday . In a statement, SpaceX called the deal the “largest committed GPU financing” . Under the agreement, an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, the New York-based private equity giant, will buy the chips and related server hardware, then lease the equipment to SpaceX. The leases will last about five to five-and-a-quarter years, beginning when each tranche of equipment is delivered, according to the filing. SpaceX expects the deal to close by year-end, subject to closing conditions, with leases starting in the first half of 2027 as the GPUs and related equipment arrive. The financing gives SpaceX another way to fund its rapidly expanding AI ambitions without relying solely on traditional debt markets. “This lease diversifies our funding sources and addresses a notable portion of the funding required to deliver on our growth plans,” SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen said in a statement Monday, noting it is seeing “less than one-year payback periods” on its AI infrastructure investments as it scales compute to power Grok and its cloud services. Apollo said the financing will help deliver Nvidia’s next-generation Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX’s “terrestrial compute buildout.” The financing comes as SpaceX ramps spending to expand its AI infrastructure, alongside its Starlink and launch businesses. The financing follows a blockbuster third quarter for SpaceX’s AI business . SpaceX’s AI segment, which includes the Grok chatbot, the Cursor coding tool, and its cloud compute business, outperformed investor expectations in the third quarter and brought in $7.6 billion of SpaceX’s $14.6 billion in revenue, more than Starlink and rocket launches combined. Capital expenditures also surged to nearly $20 billion, up from $6.9 billion a year earlier, as SpaceX races to expand its compute footprint. CFO Bret Johnse

Starlink seems to be working normally again in Ukraine
items.d: Elon Musk reportedly ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine's Starlink access.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 1:46 PM PDT · October 24, 2026 Image Credits: Jagmeet Singh / TechCrunch Anthony Ha Starlink seems to be working normally again in Ukraine SpaceX appears to have lifted restrictions on the Ukrainian military’s use of Starshield — the military-grade version of the company’s Starlink internet system. The Wall Street Journal reports that Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara told reporters that Starshield appears to be working normally again, although the military is still conducting tests and has not received an explanation for the restrictions. This follows a 10-day period when Ukrainian drones would lose internet connectivity when flying at speeds of around 100 miles per hour, resulting in the military losing control of some drones, while others became more vulnerable because they were flying more slowly. President Donald Trump reportedly called SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday and asked him to restore Starshield service. Both Trump and Musk have criticized Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, with Musk recently posting , “Zelensky has gone too far.” The WSJ previously reported that Musk ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine’s Starlink access, though some sources claimed he’d discussed it with the Trump administration first. Musk claimed in a post on X that Ukraine had “violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people.” “Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately,” Musk said. “This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.” Topics Donald Trump , Elon Musk , Government & Policy , In Brief , Space , SpaceX , Starlink , ukraine November 4 Boston Buy One Pass, Get a Second Free Cover more ground at TechCrunch’s ultimate founder bootcamp of the year by bringing your co-founder or partner for free Book before the BOGO deal expires Register Now Newsletters See More Subscribe for the industry’s biggest tech news TechCr
